verification_report.summary:
The entire supplied chapter passes verification relative to the expressly accepted inputs. The finite-dimensional definitions keep the multiplier-ideal selector separate from the continuous norm weight. The extremal kernel formula, trace identity, ideal-inclusion monotonicity, and simultaneous metric/weight gauge change are valid. The full-manifold Bernstein-Markov proof uses uniform framed charts and oscillation at most 2 epsilon, which becomes exp(epsilon m) after taking square roots. Gram differentiation gives the stated first derivative and Hessian coefficient -r! m^(1-r); the projection formula proves concavity, and Cayley-Hamilton, full-support smooth density, and connectedness prove strict negativity exactly outside constant directions. Translation and Lipschitz constants are correct. The two zero-scale conclusions follow from the mass identity. The non-Moishezon example correctly retains the complete compact flag and accounts for the degree period.

Every section of the pulled-back line bundle descends through the connected compact fibers. Equality of global singularly weighted integrals against a smooth positive volume and its smooth positive pushforward proves the selected-space correspondence. The independently weighted norms, supremum norms, Bernstein-Markov inequalities, kernels, and equally normalized measures transfer exactly. Continuous fiber averaging defines a mass-preserving, weakly continuous lift.

The supplied SGPT source and [Theorem 14.3.1](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Lectures/SGPT_final.pdf#page=483) match the application: connected compact Kahler base, pseudo-effective A, positive-mass theta-psh selector, closed non-pluripolar K, continuous w, and Bernstein-Markov probability. With trivial twisting metric, the source uses precisely the chapter's squared-norm exponent, all-positive-weight ideal comparison, quasi-everywhere obstacle, and q! normalization. Its envelope is genuine and dominates psi minus a constant; mass monotonicity makes its mass strictly positive. The exact lift yields the asserted limit, and bounded q-normalized masses give total variation convergence to zero at the n-dimensional scale when n>q.

The accepted Hopf formula and fiber probability zeta/2 give exactly (1/(2n)) MA_omega^ext(pi*E), a finite nonzero measure. The closed-curvature top product vanishes as stated. The chapter makes no unsupported extension to arbitrary singularities, general measure pullbacks, multiplier-ideal sheaf identities, upstairs envelopes, or a primitive of the raw Hermitian Monge-Ampere operator.
